collar_tag_req: All dogs in the Municipality are required to have a dog tag. Each tag is designed to stay with your dog for its entire lifetime.
dog_limit: No more than two (2) dogs may be harboured in urban areas, and no more than three (3) dogs in rural areas. Exception: A person may harbour more than 3 dogs without a kennel licence if the person keeps livestock on the same premises, the land is zoned agricultural, the dogs are licenced, and the dogs are livestock guardian and/or herding dogs.
notes: Farm friendly! Features an explicit exemption from the general 3-dog limit for livestock guardian dogs and herding dogs on agricultural properties keeping livestock. The full PDF was inaccessible to extract exact quoted definitions, but the rules are detailed on the municipal Animal Services website: https://www.huroneast.com/living-here/animal-services/

lgd_definition: “Livestock Guardian Dog” shall mean a dog that works and/or lives with domestic farm animals (e.g. cattle, sheep, poultry) to protect them while repelling predators and is used exclusively for that purpose;
herding_definition: “Herding Dog” means a dog that has been trained and is actively being used in a bona fide farming operation for the purposes of controlling livestock on the farm;
collar_tag_req: Every owner of a dog shall obtain a tag within 10 days of taking possession of a dog. Permanent dog tags are issued.
dog_limit: No person shall own, harbour, keep or permit to be kept at any one time, more than three (3) dogs per single property, location, or dwelling, with exceptions for livestock guardian or herding dogs.
notes: Very farm friendly bylaw. It provides specific exemptions for Livestock Guardian Dogs and Herding Dogs from the 3-dog limit and explicitly states that nothing in the bylaw shall apply to restrict Livestock Guardian or Herding Dogs from its duties that are a Normal Farm Practice. Such dogs have a special license fee. URL: https://howick.nyc3.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/By-laws/Township-of-Howick-Policies/Canine-Control-By-law.pdf

collar_tag_req: Effective January 1, 2026, owners are no longer required to purchase a municipal dog tag. Each owner must obtain their own tag with contact information clearly displayed, or purchase a microchip for permanent identification.
dog_limit: No person shall keep more than 3 dogs in any one dwelling unit or on any premises.
notes: Standard animal control bylaw. Barking is restricted under Noise Control By-law 19-5060. Dog tag and license fees are being eliminated entirely in 2026. No specific farm or LGD exemptions. URL: https://www.ingersoll.ca/media/mizn5bs2/january-2026-01-3989-consolidated-dog-by-law.pdf

collar_tag_req: Every owner or harbourer of a dog shall obtain a tag and keep it securely fixed on his/her dog and shall not affix the tag upon a dog other than the dog for which the said tag was issued.
dog_limit: Not specified in the retrieved text.
notes: Standard animal control bylaw focused on licensing, restraint, and dangerous dogs. Barking is restricted under the 'Nuisance Animal' clause. No farm or working dog exemptions found. Found at: https://www.killaloe-hagarty-richards.ca/sites/25/files/2025-01/21-2017%20animal%20control%20amending%2007-2011.pdf

collar_tag_req: If an Animal Licence in the form of an Animal Tag has been issued to the Keeper of an Animal, the Keeper of the Animal shall keep that Animal Tag securely affixed on the Animal at all times. Exception for hunting dogs actively hunting.
dog_limit: No strict numerical limit per household, but 4 or more dogs kept for profit/gain is considered a kennel.
notes: Standard urban animal control bylaw. Does not set a household limit on the number of dogs. Noise Control By-law (1998)-15760 prohibits the persistent barking of domestic animals at all times. No farm dog or LGD exemptions noted. URL: https://guelph.ca/wp-content/uploads/animalcontrolbylaw.pdf

collar_tag_req: On payment of the first Kitchener licence fee for a dog the owner shall be furnished with a dog tag... The owner shall keep the tag securely fixed on the dog at all times.
dog_limit: A maximum of three dogs are allowed in a household.
notes: The regulation of dogs is integrated into the Kitchener Municipal Code (Chapter 421 for Responsible Ownership). No agricultural or working dog exemptions were found. URL: https://lf.kitchener.ca/WebLinkExt/DocView.aspx?dbid=0&id=2024521

collar_tag_req: A tag shall be supplied by the Town of Kingsville for each dog in respect of which a licence fee is paid hereunder and the owner shall keep the tag securely fixed on the dog at all times.
dog_limit: No person shall harbour, keep or cause to be kept within the limits of the Town of Kingsville more than three (3) dogs unless a Kennel Licence has been issued by the Municipality.
notes: Consolidated Regulation of Dogs By-law with standard constraints and no farm/working dog exemptions. Moved to a lifetime dog-licensing program in 2024. Noise and barking is regulated under By-law 28-2006. Found at: https://www.kingsville.ca/media/d5ti4sku/103-2003-regulation-of-dogs-by-law-consolidated.pdf
